# Castos (+ Seriously Simple Podcasting WordPress plugin)

- Category: host + complement (CMS)
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://castos.com/, https://support.castos.com/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md). **Where this file and `vendors.md` differ, `vendors.md` is authoritative.**

Pro also covers "unlimited" downloads/podcasts/episodes, up to 10 team members (covers 3 seats), and up to 500 private subscribers (covers "one private/premium feed"). Growth ($49/mo) would otherwise fit seats (up to 5) and private subscribers (up to 250) but does not include video file hosting, so it fails the scenario on the video requirement alone. **Cheapest plan covering the full scenario: Pro, $99/month**, forced up from Growth specifically by the video-hosting requirement.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | [Castos Pricing](https://castos.com/pricing/) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Integration surface

- **API:** Castos REST API (token-based auth via a Castos API Token) supports create/manage Podcasts, create/manage Episodes, create/manage Private Subscribers, and list Podcast Categories — read/write for those resources. Castos states no public API exists for analytics data. Full reference is linked from the Knowledge Hub to app.castos.com/docs/api (not independently fetched in this session). [REST API technical documentation](https://support.castos.com/article/127-rest-api-technical-documentation) (2026-09-26); [Connect your WordPress site to Castos using the Castos API Token](https://support.castos.com/article/172-connect-your-wordpress-site-to-castos-using-the-castos-api-key) (2026-09-26).
- **Webhooks:** Undocumented — no webhook/event system was found on the Knowledge Hub or API overview pages checked.
- **Export formats:** RSS feed (inherent to hosting) and outbound 301 feed redirect when leaving; no explicit "bulk export" (e.g., a one-click CSV of all analytics, or a bulk media-download tool) was found documented. [Redirect your podcast's RSS feed](https://support.castos.com/article/76-redirect-your-podcasts-rss-feed) (2026-09-26).
- **SSO / auth:** Undocumented — no SSO/SAML mention found on pricing, support, or API pages checked. Team/collaborator access is via WordPress user roles (Podcast Manager, Podcast Editor) plus a Castos API Token for the WordPress-to-Castos link, not enterprise SSO. [Add your team members and podcast collaborators in WordPress](https://support.castos.com/article/75-add-your-team-members-and-podcast-collaborators-in-wordpress) (2026-09-26).
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) WordPress/SSP is the documented editing authority — "changes directly to the Castos dashboard will not push back to your WordPress site" — so episode content lives canonically in WordPress, reducing host lock-in for content itself, but podcast/episode records and hosting still live in Castos via the API-token link. (2) No public analytics API — download/listener history cannot be programmatically exported, only viewed in-dashboard, which is a lock-in risk for analytics history specifically. (3) Video hosting, transcripts, and private-subscriber counts are metered per plan tier (transcripts capped 10–100/mo below Premium; private subscribers capped 100–500 below Premium), which pushes multi-show/video use cases into higher tiers rather than blocking migration outright. (4) DAI/ad relationships are Castos-specific (Castos Ads) and MP3-only; no documented ability to export ad-insertion configuration or listener targeting data. [Quickstart Guide](https://support.castos.com/article/494-quickstart-guide-seriously-simple-podcasting-and-castos) (2026-09-26); [REST API technical documentation](https://support.castos.com/article/127-rest-api-technical-documentation) (2026-09-26); [Castos Pricing](https://castos.com/pricing/) (2026-09-26).

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Castos + Seriously Simple Podcasting is a genuine fit for Relay's "WordPress as editing authority" model: Castos' own docs state plainly that episodes must be published and managed from WordPress, not the Castos dashboard, and SSP adds two podcast-specific WordPress roles (Manager, Editor). But that's where the fit ends for Relay's harder requirements. There is no documented editorial approval workflow (draft → pending review → publish) beyond generic WordPress post statuses — nothing podcast-aware, and nothing that produces an immutable release record. Video is paywalled to the $99/mo Pro tier and Castos holds no Apple Podcasts HLS partner status, unlike several named competitors. Transcripts are metered and not documented as human-reviewable pre-publish. The API is read/write for podcasts/episodes/subscribers but explicitly excludes analytics, and no webhooks were found — a real integration gap for any event-driven build-vs-buy comparison. No dedicated comments/community or certified (vs. self-reported "compliant") analytics.

## Research notes

- The IAB Tech Lab's full "Compliant Companies" list page did not render searchable content in this session (only individual PDF certificates were discoverable via search); could not exhaustively confirm Castos is absent from all historical vintages, only that no Castos certificate appeared in search results checked, and Castos' own copy uses "compliant" rather than "certified."
- The full Castos API reference (app.castos.com/docs/api) was referenced by the Knowledge Hub article but not independently fetched — details on rate limits and full endpoint list are undocumented from sources actually loaded.
- A third-party mention of a "500 weekly downloads" threshold for the Castos Ads marketplace surfaced in search but was not present in the Castos Ads FAQ page itself as fetched; treated as unverified and excluded from the sourced finding.
- Comments/community: no Castos product page dedicated to comments/community was found; the finding is a negative (undocumented) rather than a confirmed absence.
- All pages fetched loaded successfully; none required login.
